title: Comparison Operators
summary: ==, ~=, <, >, <=, >= — compare values and produce booleans. Values of different types are never equal; tables compare by reference unless a metatable says otherwise.

details.heading: The six operators
details.body: `a == b` equal · `a ~= b` not equal · `a < b`, `a > b`, `a <= b`, `a >= b`. `< > <= >=` work on numbers and strings (lexicographic); comparing mixed types errors.

details.heading: Equality rules
details.body: Different types are never equal: `5 == "5"` is false, `nil == false` is false. Numbers, strings, booleans compare by value. Tables, functions, and Instances compare by *reference* — two identical-looking tables are not `==` unless they're the same table.

explanation.whatItIs: Operators that answer questions: are these the same? which is bigger? The answer is always a boolean you can feed into `if`.
explanation.whyItExists: Branching needs facts, and comparisons produce them.
whenToUse: `==` / `~=` for exact matches (enum states, player identity)
whenNotToUse: Don't `==` floats that came from math — compare with a tolerance: `math.abs(a - b) < 0.001`
Don't `==` two tables expecting structural equality — it's reference equality
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
5 == 5        --> true
5 == "5"      --> false   (different types)
"cat" < "dog" --> true    (alphabetical)
{} == {}      --> false   (two different tables)

local t = {}
t == t        --> true    (same table)
```
tips: `~=` is 'not equal' — there is no `!=` in Luau
Comparing an Instance to a stored reference is the standard 'is this the same object?' check
For approximate numeric equality, write a helper: `local function near(a, b) return math.abs(a - b) < 1e-3 end`
commonMistakes: Using `=` (assignment) instead of `==` in conditions — syntax error
Comparing Vector3/CFrame with `==` works (value equality), but floats inside still suffer precision issues

examples.title: Everyday comparisons
examples.code:
local health = 0
print(health <= 0)        --> true
print(health == nil)      --> false

local state = Enum.HumanoidStateType.Running
print(state == Enum.HumanoidStateType.Running)   --> true

-- Reference equality for tables:
local a = {1, 2}
local b = {1, 2}
print(a == b)             --> false
print(a == a)             --> true
